title: The Wellness Dental Practice
html:
Why Dentists Are Becoming the First Line of Whole-Patient Health

The next opportunity for a dental practice may begin with a question a patient has never thought to ask: Can you help me feel better? Jaw discomfort, muscle tension, and difficulty chewing already bring that question into dental care. A practice that responds with a broader understanding of pain and function can build on an existing relationship while creating a new reason for patients to return.

The ADA recognizes oral health as integral to systemic health.1 For dentists, a wellness model puts that relationship into daily practice. Regular visits provide opportunities to recognize concerns, understand how symptoms affect daily life, and connect patients with appropriate care. Some practices can build on that foundation through an affiliated wellness clinic, extending their services from facial function to other muscle groups under qualified clinical oversight.

Address Pain and Function Together

A useful clinical framework separates relief of an acute episode of discomfort from management of persistent pain or neuromuscular dysfunction. The treatments may overlap, but the goals differ. A patient seeking relief today may also need a longer-term plan for muscle function. Diagnosis, symptom duration, and functional limitations should guide the choice of technology and the sequence of care.

EMVITAL (BTL Aesthetics) brings a laser-based approach to symptomatic relief. Its intended use includes topical heating for temporary relief of muscle and joint pain and stiffness, minor arthritis pain and muscle spasm, along with temporary muscle relaxation and increased local circulation.2 That makes it relevant to an acute pain presentation, while also giving it a role in temporary relief of symptoms associated with longer-standing conditions such as minor arthritis pain.

EMFACE creates a direct connection to dentistry through its functional indications. The platform combines synchronized radiofrequency and HIFES technology and is FDA-cleared for treatment of TMJ dysfunction and associated pain, relief of muscle spasm, muscle re-education, increased local blood flow, and maintenance or improvement of mandibular range of motion.3 For appropriately selected patients with persistent jaw symptoms, those uses support a conversation about both comfort and function.

The dental examination remains essential. Temporomandibular disorders can involve chewing muscles, joints, or both, and symptoms may extend into the face or neck.4 A treatment plan should identify the problem and establish meaningful goals, such as more comfortable chewing or improved jaw movement. EMVITAL and EMFACE offer different approaches within that plan, allowing clinicians to consider symptomatic relief alongside functional care.

Barry Applegate, DMD, of Applegate Dentistry & MedSpa in Covington, Ky, has processes in place to clearly explain the innovative services and benefits now offered by BTL Aesthetics.

“We’ve put effort into more than adding technology. We’ve developed treatment books, custom educational videos, and clear pricing packages so patients can understand their options and our team has the tools to explain them. Patient education is part of the service, not something that happens after the treatment is sold,” Dr. Applegate said.

Tina Chandra, DDS, who is a LVI-trained physiologic dentist in Ocala, Fla, has also become a leader in exploring how advanced technology can support individuals experiencing TMJ and facial discomfort. She initiated studies investigating the use of BTL technologies, including EMFACE and the EMVITAL laser, for TMJ-related concerns. These technologies utilize muscle stimulation, radio frequency, and photobiomodulation to support facial muscle relaxation, jaw movement, circulation, and overall patient comfort.

“With EMFACE and EMVITAL, it has completely elevated my TMJ care for my patients,” she said. “Whether they have limited opening, clicking, popping, headaches, or just simply can’t chew their food, a quick few sessions of EMFACE and the laser alleviate the pain and discomfort so quickly. Never have I had technology that works that fast for my patients. Using both these procedures before I make the orthotic or bite guard for my patient, helps dramatically. It’s a game changer!”

Expand Beyond the Face With a Clinical Purpose

When a wellness clinic begins treating other muscle groups, EMSCULPT NEO brings neuromuscular applications to the model. Its rehabilitative uses include stimulation of neuromuscular tissue in the arms or legs, muscle re-education, prevention or retardation of disuse atrophy, and maintenance or increase of range of motion.5 These uses make muscle function a reason to consider the platform alongside its established aesthetic applications.

Its role also extends to nerves. EMSCULPT NEO is intended to stimulate peripheral nerves for relief of chronic intractable pain, post-traumatic pain, post-surgical pain, and chronic painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy in the lower extremities, in patients 18 and older.5 The appropriate clinical message is pain relief through peripheral nerve stimulation, with patient selection and treatment directed by a qualified provider.

EMVITAL becomes an important part of this broader offering because muscle and joint discomfort can accompany the concerns that bring patients into a wellness clinic. Its indication for temporary relief of minor arthritis pain adds another relevant application. A clinician may consider pain relief and neuromuscular treatment within the same overall plan, selecting each service for the patient’s needs and its applicable indications.

“TMD pain is not just confined to the jaw. It affects our whole upper quadrant component of our body. The photobiomodulation EMVITAL laser is very versatile to help with neck, shoulder, and back pain as well reducing inflammation and stiffness quickly. It helps so much with muscle re-education and pairs well with the EMFACE muscle stimulation,” Dr. Chandra added.

Make Treatment Practical

Clinical expansion must also fit the working day. EMFACE and EMSCULPT NEO use hands-free applicators, so treatment delivery does not require a practitioner to continuously hold and move a handpiece. EMVITAL offers a hands-free option for larger areas and a small handpiece for more focused treatment. That flexibility helps match a treatment approach to the size and location of the area being addressed. Hands-free delivery still requires patient monitoring and clinical supervision. Its operational value is the ability to organize treatment around trained staff, appropriate room use, and a predictable workflow. Practices should assess the actual staff time required for screening, setup, monitoring, and followup before deciding how a wellness service fits their capacity.

“Through our Dental Preceptorship Program, we help other dental teams think through how these services fit into their own practices—from patient conversations to treatment presentation and daily workflow,” added Dr. Applegate.

Kristen Graham, DDS, is the founder of Biological Wellness in Arizona. She is a big proponent of using today’s technologies in the dental office to have an impact on patients’ overall well being.

“We care for whole humans, and oral and facial health are inseparable from the rest of the body,” Dr. Graham said. “The relationship between the jaw and pelvic floor is an emerging example. The deep fascial network, often discussed through the ‘deep front line’ model, offers a proposed anatomical framework linking the pelvic floor, diaphragm, neck, and jaw. Early research has found changes in pelvic floor muscle activity following manual treatment of the jaw muscles, although the mechanisms and long-term clinical significance need further study.

“Stress and anxiety also deserve attention because they can influence muscle tension and the experience of pain. Dentists bring expertise in oral and facial anatomy, jaw function, and patient relationships that positions us to recognize these broader patterns and coordinate care. Supporting optimal dental health means understanding the human attached to the smile.”

Keep the Patient Well and the Practice Healthy

A wellness clinic can create a cash-pay revenue stream while broadening the care available within an established patient relationship. Someone whose needs previously took them outside the practice may now have an appropriate option within its coordinated clinical team. This creates an opportunity to retain more of the patient’s care and strengthen continuity, while preserving referrals whenever specialist evaluation or treatment is needed.

The financial case should be built on clinical value and realistic demand. Patients need clear explanations of treatment goals, likely limitations, and fees. Practices need qualified providers, outcome tracking, and a structure consistent with professional scope and state requirements. “These technologies give us different tools within that broader approach. EMFACE Functional addresses TMJ dysfunction and associated pain and movement limitations, while EMVITAL offers temporary relief of muscle and joint discomfort,” Dr. Graham explained. “Additionally, we have EMSCULPT NEO, which brings muscle re-education and rehabilitation into the picture.”

“My goal is to help patients feel more comfortable, capable, and confident while supporting the oral, facial, and overall health that allows them to live fully,” she added.

For dentistry, whole-patient wellness begins with a familiar strength: knowing the person who sits in the chair. Extending that relationship through thoughtful pain and muscle care can give patients more reasons to stay connected to the practice. The goal is to keep the patient well and the practice healthy.

“Our philosophy is reflected in our practice’s message: inspired by patients, driven by science. As we bring dentistry, aesthetics, and wellness together, we’re building on the trust our patients already place in us to help them take a step forward in their wellness journey with us,” Dr. Applegate concluded.
